reason: Hierarchy is prominently emphasized throughout this narrative (2 Kings 5). The text repeatedly describes and highlights hierarchical relationships and positions: Naaman is introduced as 'a great man before his lord' (אִישׁ גָּדוֹל לִפְנֵי אֲדֹנָיו), a military commander (שַׂר־צְבָא) under the king of Aram. The captured servant girl addresses her mistress (גְּבִרְתָּה) with deference. Multiple characters—Naaman, servants, and officials—operate within and acknowledge clear chains of command and authority. The narrative structure itself reinforces hierarchy: the king commands Naaman, Naaman seeks the prophet, the prophet instructs through messengers, and servants advise their master. While the theological climax involves Naaman humbling himself before spiritual authority, the social structure of hierarchy is woven throughout the entire narrative as a fundamental organizing principle.
